https://www.lahainanews.com/wire/?catego.text: Social media influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate arrested in Miami, US Marshals Service tells AP By AP | Jul 19, 2026 FILE - Andrew Tate, right, and his brother Tristan arrive an event, April 11, 2026, in Miami. (AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson, Pool, File) By ALANNA DURKIN RICHER Associated Press Influencer brothers Andrew and Tristan Tate, whose social media empire promoting wealth, male dominance and misogyny has made them among the world’s most polarizing internet personalities, were arrested Saturday in Miami as British authorities sought their extradition on rape and sex trafficking charges. The brothers were taken into custody by the U.S. Marshals Service on a sealed warrant, agency spokesperson Brady McCarron told The Associated Press, placing the United States at the center of an international legal saga that has stretched from Romania to Britain. Britain is seeking their extradition on rape and trafficking charges British prosecutors announced Saturday that they were seeking the brothers’ extradition on charges alleging they raped and trafficked women between 2010 and 2017. The dual U.S. and British citizens moved to Romania in 2016. They were arrested there in 2022, accused of participating in schemes to lure women for sexual exploitation. They denied those allegations and the Romanian case hasn’t gone forward because of legal and procedural problems. Last year, they were allowed to leave Romania and flew to Florida on a private jet. The brothers are expected to appear in Miami’s federal court early next week, according to a person familiar with the matter who spoke to on the condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive law enforcement operations. The pending charges in the United Kingdom accused the brothers of abusing women in an area north of London, where they grew up. Their lawyers had said they denied the allegations. Joseph McBride, an attorney representing the Tate brothers, said in a phone interview Saturday evening that he has not been able to speak with his clients but called the new charges out of the U.K. “filth and slander” intended to derail defamation lawsuits filed by the brothers in the U.S. “They’re pulling out all the stops to make sure these guys never get their day in court,” McBride said. “We are confident that once a competent judge sees the facts, and once the Department of Justice confronts this egregious abuse of its own authority, Andrew and Tristan Tate will walk free. America does not do Britain’s political dirty work.” Tate has been banned from social media platforms for hate speech Andrew Tate, 39, first reached a mainstream audience as a contestant on the U.K. reality television show “Big Brother” in 2016. He was removed from the show when a video surfaced that appeared to show Tate assaulting a woman. He and his brother Tristan Tate, 38, are vocal supporters of U.S. President Donald Trump. Andrew Tate has amassed over 10 million followers on X but has been banned from platforms like YouTube, TikTok and Instagram for violating hate speech guidelines. His most widely condemned rhetoric includes comments that women who are sexually assaulted should bear some responsibility for their attacks, graphic descriptions of how he might attack women and criticisms of people who seek treatment for mental illness. The Tate brothers have consistently denied allegations of abuse and human trafficking, claiming that violent and misogynistic statements have been taken out of context or were intended as jokes. In a statement Saturday, the U.K.’s Crown Prosecution Services said that in addition to the charges publicly announced against the brothers in 2025, involving alleged crimes against three women, it was bringing a total of 38 new charges related to “four further victims.” Both brothers are accused of rape and human trafficking. Andrew Tate faces an additional charge of profiting from prostitution, and 19 charges “for offences relating to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography,” according to U.K. authorities. “There is no place for male violence against women and girls, and we will continue to work tirelessly to support victims and investigate all reports made to us,” said Karena Thomas, an assistant chief constable of the Bedfordshire Police, which investigated the case. ___ Associated Press writer Savannah Peters in Santa Fe, New Mexico contributed to this report. https://www.theguardian.com/politics/202.text: Caroline Voaden said the incident had happened after Nigel Farage told her to ‘let me past’ and she replied he should ‘wait his turn like everyone else’. Composite: House of Commons; Stefan Rousseau/PA View image in fullscreen Caroline Voaden said the incident had happened after Nigel Farage told her to ‘let me past’ and she replied he should ‘wait his turn like everyone else’. Composite: House of Commons; Stefan Rousseau/PA Nigel Farage Female Lib Dem MP accuses Nigel Farage of shoving her in parliament Caroline Voaden says the Reform UK leader grabbed her by the arm and tried to push past her in incident in May UK politics live – latest updates Rowena Mason and Peter Walker Thu 29 Oct 2026 13.54 EDT First published on Thu 29 Oct 2026 10.16 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A female Liberal Democrat MP has accused Nigel Farage of shoving her aside at the state opening of parliament after which one of her male colleagues intervened. Caroline Voaden gave her account of the incident in May this year after Farage revealed on Wednesday that there had been a “physical altercation” in parliament which meant he had decided to avoid the budget. Voaden told the Guardian: “He was trying to get out of the chamber and instead of just asking if he could go past, he said ‘let me past’. I turned round and said ‘no, you can wait your turn like everyone else’. He grabbed me by the arm or the shoulder, pushed me to one side and tried to push past me. One of my colleagues tried to stop him because he thought I was going to fall down the stairs. And then we all shuffled down. “Quite deliberately, he grabbed me by the arm from behind and pushed me to one side so that I fell into a colleague or the wall on the other side. I was really taken aback and really angry because I think you just don’t behave like that in any workplace, let alone the chamber of the House of Commons. It was rude. It was nasty.” Voaden said she had complained to the sergeant at arms who she believed had written to Farage asking him to apologise. She also raised it with the speaker. “Nothing ever came of it,” she said. View image in fullscreen Caroline Voaden speaks in parliament Photograph: House of Commons A Reform UK source said it was “not true at all, it was the Lib Dem MPs being aggressive towards Nigel. This is typical Lib Dem dishonesty in an attempt to stay relevant”. The male Lib Dem MP who intervened is understood to be Max Wilkinson, with sources saying he put a hand on Farage’s shoulder, “fairly gently” grabbed him and said he could not do that to another MP. Reform sources also suggested a video from the Commons shows her account was wrong, but the Lib Dems say the incident took place before the footage starts. The row erupted after the Reform leader said on Wednesday that he had skipped John Healey’s speech in the House of Commons due to his seat reservation having been moved, so he decided to give it a “wide berth” in order to “avoid conflict” in the chamber. He claimed that he had been involved in a “physical altercation” with another MP on the day of the state opening of parliament in May. It later emerged his reservation had been removed by Commons staff as it did not have the proper date stamp. Nigel Farage skips budget in Commons over seating ‘altercation’ concerns Read more Daisy Cooper, the Lib Dem deputy leader, had earlier revealed to Sky News that her party’s MPs were involved in the May incident mentioned by Farage. Cooper told Sky News: “My understanding – I didn’t see it, I wasn’t there – but my understanding is that he physically shoved one of our female MPs out of the way, and that one of our male MPs then challenged him on that. “I didn’t see it, I didn’t witness what happened, but that was several months ago. “And let’s be really clear: it’s Reform UK that had a problem at their conference with bundling female journalists and members out of their hall. So, we’ll take no lessons from them on this.” Afterwards, Voaden posted on social media, saying: “We both know that’s not true Nigel don’t we? “I’m still waiting for the apology you were required to write to me … Though I won’t hold my breath.” When asked for a response to the accusations, Robert Jenrick, Reform’s shadow chancellor, said: “You know what? I am sick to death of these pathetic Westminster debates. “The thing about Reform politicians is, yeah, we love parliament, the institution of parliament. I go there every day. I speak in parliament. I represent my constituents. “But I’m much more interested about, actually, the issues, trying to change this country, getting out and about outside of the bubble. And I’m not interested in even responding, dignifying the nonsense that Daisy Cooper is talking about there.” Explore more on these topics Nigel Farage Liberal Democrats Reform UK Budget news Share Reuse this content More on this story More on this story Nigel Farage skips budget in Commons over seating ‘altercation’ concerns Schrödinger’s racism, Nige’s latest wheeze to try to dodge his associates’ bigotry Reform UK braces for Farage standards verdict over undeclared £5m gift Nige seems tired and bored of himself as Kemi conjures a telepathic budget Farage claim that £5m was reward for Brexit was ‘not press office line’, close aide says Jenrick claims Farage has done more to stand against racism than ‘almost anybody’ Just as Saint Nige thought it was safe to reappear, along comes pesky ITV Nigel Farage questioned by standards commissioner over £5m gift Burnham’s reopening of Brexit debate is ‘biggest boost in my career’, says Farage To the people voting for Nigel Farage: is this really the finger you want on the red button?
